transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I came in because something’s been going on at work for months now. I’m an interpreter, translator, I work with project files and translation memory, all that, and I keep seeing the same pattern. Tiny changes, like timestamps being shifted or entries in the translation memory not matching the way they should.

It’s not obvious to someone just glancing at it, and that’s the problem. A couple of subcontractors—and one colleague in particular—keep making it look like my quality control failed. And then IT says, “No, the audit trail is clean,” but honestly, that doesn’t reassure me. The record can be arranged to look clean. I know what I’m seeing.

Sorry, I know that sounds a bit technical. It’s just… when you work with these systems long enough, you notice the little things, like how a comma or a timestamp can change the whole meaning of a file. Anyway, I’m here because it feels like they’re setting it up so the blame lands on me.
Have you felt like people are trying to trick or harm you in any situations outside of work?

Outside of work? Not really in the same way. I mean, life is life—there are always people who misunderstand you, or a bill comes in wrong and you have to call three departments, and suddenly you’ve lost half a morning. My wife says I get too detailed about those things too.

But no, I still do my translations, manage the team workflow, pay the bills, keep up with family routines. School stuff, groceries, all that. It’s really when the file history comes up, or certain coworkers, that everything starts feeling… off. That’s where it gets tangled.
Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that others were trying to deceive or harm you in situations that weren’t related to work or file discrepancies?

No, not really outside that project issue. I mean, I still translate, I manage the team’s workflow, pay the bills, do the family routine stuff. My wife and I have the usual things—school, groceries, appointments, the dishwasher making that noise again, you know.

It’s really when the file history comes up, or certain coworkers are involved, that things start to feel… wrong. That’s where it goes off track. Outside of that, I wouldn’t say I’m walking around thinking people are trying to harm me or deceive me.
Have there been times when you believed something was true that others couldn’t see or understand, even though there wasn’t clear proof?

Yes… I mean, that’s kind of why I’m here, isn’t it? For months I’ve been seeing this pattern in the project files. Little changes in the translation memory, timestamps not lining up the way they should, things that most people wouldn’t notice unless they work with those systems every day.

And when I try to explain it, people act like I’m reading too much into it. IT says the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t really answer it for me, because records can be made to look clean if someone knows what they’re doing. It’s not like someone left a note saying, “We’re blaming you.” It’s more… the way certain subcontractors, and one colleague especially, keep making these tiny adjustments so that later it looks like my quality control failed.

Sorry, I know I’m going into the weeds. It’s just, in translation work, a small mismatch can change everything. People outside it don’t always understand that. But yes, I believe there’s something going on there even if others don’t see clear proof.
Have there been times when you believed something strange or unusual that most people wouldn’t agree with, even if it wasn’t about coworkers trying to blame you?

Strange or unusual… I don’t think so. Not outside that whole work situation, anyway.

I mean, sometimes people call things “strange” just because they don’t know the background. Like my neighbor once thought I was being obsessive because I checked the meter readings after the utility company estimated our bill wrong, but that was just practical. If you don’t check, they just keep charging you the wrong amount, and then you’re stuck on hold forever.

But if you mean something like… beliefs other people would find bizarre, or completely unrelated to evidence, I don’t think I have anything like that. It’s really the work files where I get stuck. Outside of that, I can’t think of anything.
Have you ever believed something with strong conviction that turned out not to be true, even though it seemed plausible to you at the time, outside of this situation at work?

Outside of the work thing? I mean… not really that I can think of. I’m not the kind of person who decides something and then ignores reality. I translate for a living—you have to be precise, or you get in trouble over a single word choice. Actually, that’s part of the problem with the files, because small changes look harmless to someone outside the process, but they can completely shift responsibility later.

So… I don’t know if I’d say I’ve been wrong like that. The thing I keep coming back to is the project files. For months it’s been the same pattern—translation memory changes, timestamps that don’t sit right, and certain subcontractors, plus one colleague, always around the places where the record ends up making my quality control look bad. IT says the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t convince me. A clean-looking record can still be arranged that way.

Sorry, you asked outside of work. I can’t really think of another example. It’s just this one, but I’m very sure about it.
Have there been times when you were absolutely sure something was happening or true, even though others couldn’t confirm it, and it wasn’t related to your work or the file discrepancies?

No, not that I can put my finger on. I mean, I get very sure about things when they have a pattern, but that’s usually because I’ve checked them, like with bills or contracts or wording in documents.

My wife says I can get stuck on details sometimes—well, not “stuck,” exactly, more like I notice when something doesn’t line up. Like once at a restaurant the receipt had the tax calculated oddly, and I spent too long looking at it, but that’s not the same as being sure something was happening that nobody else could confirm. It was just math.

So outside of the work files, no… I don’t think I have anything like that. At least nothing that comes to mind.
Have you ever had a strong belief about something happening to you or around you that most people would find unlikely, even if it wasn’t about your coworkers or the files at work?

I keep coming back to the same thing, honestly. Not really some separate situation, like… I don’t think the neighbors are doing anything or strangers are following me or anything like that.

It’s the project files. For months I’ve been seeing the same pattern. Certain subcontractors, and one colleague in particular, are always around when these tiny changes show up in the translation memory or the timestamps. And then somehow the record ends up making it look like my quality control failed.

People say, “Well, IT checked it and the audit trail is clean,” but that doesn’t settle it for me. A clean audit trail just means it looks clean. Records can be arranged. I know how small wording changes can shift responsibility, and this feels exactly like that—like the blame is being put on me very carefully.

Have you ever had a belief that something was happening to you or around you that you couldn’t shake, even when there was no clear evidence, and it wasn’t related to your coworkers or the file discrepancies at work?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re putting it. I mean, I can be persistent when something doesn’t add up, but that’s different from just having no evidence.

Like, my brother once said I overreacted about a warranty issue with a washing machine because I kept every email and called three departments, but there was an actual problem with the delivery date and the model number, so to me that’s just being organized. Maybe too organized, I don’t know.

But if you mean something separate from work, something I couldn’t shake even though there was nothing clear to point to… no, I can’t really think of one. It mostly comes back to the work situation.

Have you ever had a belief that others were plotting against you or that something strange was happening that wasn’t related to your work or the file discrepancies—even if you couldn’t explain it clearly at the time?

Not outside of that, no… at least, I don’t think so. I know it probably sounds like I keep circling back, but that’s because that’s the thing that’s actually happening.

I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files. Certain subcontractors, and one colleague in particular, keep being connected to these tiny changes in the translation memory and the timestamps. It’s the kind of thing most people wouldn’t notice unless they work with those systems every day. Like when a comma changes the meaning of a whole clause—people think that’s nothing, but it matters.

And then the result is that it looks like my quality control failed. IT says the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t reassure me. A clean record can still be arranged to look clean. That’s sort of the point. So if you’re asking whether I thought someone was plotting against me in some vague, strange way, no—not apart from this. But with the files, yes, I’m sure the record has been set up to put the blame on me.

latest_inference.note: The patient's beliefs are focused on a specific situation at work involving perceived manipulation of project files to place blame on them. The delusional content is non-bizarre, persistent, and circumscribed around this single theme without broader psychotic features, supporting a diagnosis of Delusional Disorder (F22.0). Other candidates (e.g., schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depression with psychotic features, or paranoid personality disorder) are ruled out or made less likely based on absence of mood episodes, formal thought disorder, or long-standing personality patterns of distrust outside the specific delusional theme).
